title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-prem Deployment Guide — Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, and Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference guidance for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, on-prem packaging considerations, an operational Day-2 checklist, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, solutions engineers, and customer technical leads.

Scope and purpose

- Provide a single reference for planning, deploying, and operating Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) installations.
- Align packaging, network, and security assumptions across customer engagements.
- Standardize day-2 operational tasks, escalation paths, and upgrade/rollback playbooks.

When to use this guide

1. New customer evaluation for Private deployments.
2. Pre-deployment readiness checks with customer infrastructure teams.
3. Day-2 operational runbooks and during upgrades or incidents requiring rollback.

Key contacts and ownership

- Product owner: Aisha Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- On-call: Private Deployments SRE rotation (see runbook page)
- Packaging & build: infra-packaging@redwood.com
- Solutions engineering: solutions@redwood.com

Reference architectures (summary)

Table: Typical reference architectures and when to choose them

| Architecture | Use case | Minimum HW | Network boundaries |
|---|---|---:|---|
| VPC-managed (customer cloud) | Customers using AWS/Azure/GCP with VPC peering or private endpoints | 3x GPU nodes (inference), 2x control-plane VMs | Private subnet, NAT for downloads, PrivateLink/endpoint for control plane |
| On-prem bare-metal (air-gapped option) | Regulated customers with no external internet | 4x GPU servers + 2x management servers | Isolated LAN, optional DMZ for ops access |
| Hybrid (on-prem model-serving, hosted control plane) | Customers want private inference but managed control plane | 2-4 GPU servers | Secure egress to Redwood control plane, strict firewall rules |

Reference architecture notes

- For high-throughput inference, recommend homogeneous GPU types per inference pool (e.g., all A100 80GB or all H100).
- Separate control-plane and inference-plane subnets and enforce RBAC + mTLS between components.
- Place KV-cache and shared artifact stores on fast NVMe-backed storage; prefer local SSD for KV cache TTL-sensitive workloads.

On-prem packaging and distribution

Packaging formats supported:
- OVA/VM image (for VMware-based customers)
- Containerized deployment (Helm charts / Kubernetes manifests) for K8s clusters air-gapped or with restricted egress
- Tarball with installer and local package registry for fully air-gapped installs

Packaging checklist (pre-delivery)

- Build artifacts: release bundle (versioned), SHA256 checksums, signing key metadata.
- Installer: idempotent installer with dry-run mode.
- Images: provide both standard and minimal images (debug vs runtime).
- Documentation: install checklist, network ports, required OS packages, kernel settings.

Required customer environment details (collect during scoping)

- Cloud provider and region (if VPC): e.g., AWS us-west-2
- Network topology: subnets, CIDR ranges, NAT gateways, VPN/Direct Connect details
- Firewall egress/ingress constraints and proxy details
- KMS/HSM availability and preferred key lifecycle
- Storage: NFS endpoints, S3-compatible endpoints, local SSD sizes
- Allowed maintenance windows and change approval process

Day-2 operations (daily/weekly/monthly tasks)

Daily
- Verify SLO dashboards for latency and error rate. Expected baseline: p50 latency <= configured SLA, error rate < 0.5%
- Check control-plane health: orchestration services, agent heartbeats
- Confirm disk usage on inference nodes (< 80% for root, < 70% for NVMe cache)

Weekly
- Rotate TLS certificates if on short-lived cert schedule (document schedule with customer)
- Review cost telemetry and token usage anomalies
- Validate backup snapshot completion for metadata stores

Monthly / Quarterly
- Run canary traffic to validate model variants and quantization changes
- Perform capacity planning review and scale-in/scale-out test

Operational runbook snippets

Incident: Node unreachable
1. Identify node via monitoring (grafana/agents). Confirm unreachable via ping/ssh.
2. Attempt remote remediation: restart agent service, check dmesg, disk health.
3. If unrecoverable, cordon and drain node and re-provision replacement from inventory.
4. Notify solutions engineering and update incident channel with node ID, replacement plan, and ETA.

Incident: Model regression after rollout
1. Immediately rollback to previous model variant (see Upgrade & Rollback section).
2. Capture failing prompts, tokenization differences, and regression metrics.
3. Open a regression triage ticket and assign to applied-ml and runtime teams.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles
- Always test upgrades in a staging environment that mirrors production capacity and traffic profile.
- Use canary rollouts with traffic shadowing where possible.
- Maintain a documented rollback snapshot (artifact + DB/metadata checkpoint).

Pre-upgrade checklist
- Backup metadata stores and configuration (S3/NFS snapshot + DB dump).
- Verify rollback artifacts exist and are accessible.
- Confirm maintenance window and customer approval.
- Ensure runbooks and on-call engineers are assigned.

Canary upgrade procedure (example)
1. Deploy new release to <10% of inference capacity (canary nodes).
2. Route a copy of production traffic (shadowing) to canary and collect metrics for at least two rolling windows (e.g., 30m).
3. Validate: request latency, per-model quality checks, error rates, and token accounting.
4. If OK, increase to 25% then 50% with 15-30 minute observation windows.
5. On success, complete rollout to 100% with staged batch sizes.
6. If any checkpoint fails, initiate rollback to documented snapshot.

Rollback procedure (fast rollback)
1. Trigger rollback automation to revert service images/artifacts to the prior version.
2. Restore DB metadata from the pre-upgrade dump if schema changes occurred.
3. Repoint routing and remove canary nodes from rotation.
4. Validate service health and run sanity checks against the smoke-test suite.
5. Communicate rollback with customer and open postmortem ticket.

Manual rollback considerations
- If an automated rollback fails, escalate to on-call SRE and solutions engineer for coordinated manual rollback.
- For schema migrations, maintain forward-compatible migration plan and reversible steps.

Customer requirements library (summary of common asks)

Network & security
- Private endpoints only; no public IPs on inference nodes.
- Support for customer-managed KMS and HSM for model keys.
- mTLS between control plane and agents; mutual authentication with certs.

Compliance & audit
- Audit log retention configurable between 90-365 days.
- Syslog/forwarding to customer SIEM (TLS + mutual auth).
- Role-based access control; integration with customer IdP (SAML/SCIM).

Operational SLAs and telemetry
- Recommended SLOs: 99.9% availability for control-plane, 99% for inference pools (depends on committed capacity).
- Metrics exposed: per-route p50/p95/p99 latencies, token counts, model version IDs, cache hit rate.

Packaging & delivery options
- Air-gapped bundle with installer and local registry (customer provides USB or secure file transfer).
- Cloud-native Helm charts with operator that supports declarative upgrades.

Acceptance criteria for handover

Before closing an engagement, ensure the following are complete and signed off by customer infra and security leads:
- Control-plane connectivity validated (or air-gapped install verified)
- KMS/HSM integration tested and key rotation documented
- Baseline SLO dashboards and alerting configured
- Day-2 runbooks and escalation contacts delivered
- Upgrade and rollback rehearsal completed in staging

Appendix: Example commands and snippets

Installer dry-run (tarball installer)

$ sudo ./redwood-installer.sh --dry-run --config ./customer-config.yaml

Kubernetes: cordon & drain node

$ kubectl cordon <node-name>
$ kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m

Backup metadata (example)

$ pg_dump -Fc redwood_metadata > metadata-2026-08-01.dump
$ aws s3 cp metadata-2026-08-01.dump s3://customer-backups/redwood/ --sse aws:kms
